jobs.title: Director of Software Engineering
jobs.description:
Description

Job Summary:

We are looking for a visionary and technically strong Director of Software Engineering to lead our engineering teams in building scalable, secure, and high-performance software solutions. This role is pivotal in shaping our technical strategy, driving engineering excellence, and delivering innovative products in a fast-paced, tech-driven environment.

Responsibilities

Leadership & Strategy
Define and execute the engineering roadmap in alignment with company goals and product strategy, and technical leadership.
Lead and mentor tech leads, software and QA engineers across multiple teams.
Foster a high-performance culture focused on innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Establish clear goals, metrics, and accountability frameworks for engineering teams

Technical Oversight
Help guide architectural decisions and ensure adherence to modern software engineering principles.
Champion best practices in software design, testing, deployment, and operations.
Evaluate and implement new technologies to improve scalability, reliability, and developer productivity.

Project & Product Delivery
Collaborate with leadership, design, and the Product Delivery Office to deliver high-quality software on time and within scope.
Strong command of SDLC best practices, agile methodologies, and application lifecycle management
Ensure robust monitoring, alerting, and incident response practices are in place.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
10+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years in a leadership role.
Proven experience leading engineering teams in a technical product or SaaS company.
Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills
Deep understanding of cloud-native architectures (AWS and Azure), microservices, and distributed systems.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence across departments.
Experience with Agile, Scrum, or SAFe methodologies.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with security and compliance standards (e.g., FedRAMP, PCI, etc.)
Background in AI/ML, data engineering, or platform engineering is a plus.

About the Organization Eccalon provides global solutions to the most challenging technological issues of the 21st-century, and our evolving portfolio spans five major markets: Machine Learning, Cybersecurity, Aerospace & Defense, Material Sciences, Advance Manufacturing, Sports Science, Biotechnology, and Health & Life Sciences.

Why Join Us?

Eccalon's Executives foster a supportive work environment allowing our teams to thrive, and have a fierce dedication to innovation, security, and people. Our culture is built on inclusion, teamwork, trust, and we are committed to offering career advancement opportunities to all employees. Encouraging a healthy and balanced life, we offer an extensive benefits package to support the wellness of our employees and their families. You will be joining a team of innovators, working with cutting edge technologies, supporting mission critical projects, and making an impact.

Apply today to advance your career!

jobs.title: Vice President of Engineering Projects
jobs.description:
Company Description
Invescorp World™ designs and manages how verified real-world assets are structured, issued, and settled in private, highly controlled environments. The organization focuses on compliance-first financial infrastructure, supporting internal value systems and verified asset-backed coins distributed only through private and OTC channels for qualified participants. Its operating model emphasizes strict admission criteria, selective access, and final settlement, avoiding speculation and public trading environments. Key capabilities include real-world asset structuring, private issuance and settlement, authorized wallet systems, and sovereign private blockchain solutions. Invescorp World™ is powered by InvesChain™, a sovereign, private blockchain network built for long-term value systems and rigorous control.
Role Description
The Engineering Projects Vice President will lead complex engineering programs and project portfolios that support Invescorp World’s asset structuring, blockchain infrastructure, and private issuance platforms. This full-time, remote role oversees end-to-end project lifecycles, including scoping, technical planning, resource allocation, budgeting, risk management, and delivery of mission-critical systems. Responsibilities include aligning engineering initiatives with strategic business priorities, coordinating cross-functional technical teams, and ensuring compliance-first design across infrastructure and products. The role will define project governance standards, implement performance metrics, and drive continuous improvement in engineering processes and tools. The Engineering Projects Vice President will also collaborate closely with senior leadership to translate high-level strategy into executable roadmaps and to communicate progress and outcomes to stakeholders.
Qualifications

Candidates should possess strong Program Management and Project Management skills to oversee multiple concurrent engineering initiatives and complex technical portfolios.
Candidates should possess robust Analytical Skills and Strategic Planning capabilities to interpret data, anticipate risks, and design long-term engineering roadmaps aligned with business goals.
Candidates should possess solid Budgeting and resource management skills to plan, control, and optimize project costs and investments across diverse engineering programs.
Extensive experience leading engineering or technology projects in financial services, blockchain, fintech, or other highly regulated environments is beneficial.
Proven ability to manage distributed, remote teams, with excellent communication, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills.
Familiarity with blockchain networks, asset-backed digital instruments, and compliance-driven infrastructure design is advantageous.
Advanced degree in engineering, computer science, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent senior-level industry experience.
Demonstrated track record of delivering complex, high-impact technology projects on time and within scope, with a focus on security, reliability, and long-term value.

jobs.title: Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The hiring organization is seeking a strategic and hands-on Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
to lead the technology capabilities that keep digital products, cloud platforms, and internal teams secure, reliable, and productive.

This role oversees cloud infrastructure, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), production operations, bot mitigation, corporate IT, and helpdesk support, while providing architectural leadership across cloud platforms, networking, identity, observability, and operational tooling. This position spans both internal employee technology and the production infrastructure supporting high-traffic, customer-facing applications.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Lead teams responsible for cloud infrastructure, SRE, production operations, corporate IT, helpdesk, and bot mitigation, establishing ownership, operational standards, service-level objectives (SLOs), escalation procedures, and performance metrics.
Develop managers, technical leads, and IT staff through coaching, career development, and building a culture of accountability, documentation, automation, and continuous improvement.
Build quarterly and annual infrastructure roadmaps aligned with business priorities, growth, security, reliability, and cost, partnering with engineering, product, data, marketing, finance, HR, legal, and executive leadership.
Own the reliability, scalability, security, performance, and cost-effectiveness of cloud infrastructure, primarily within AWS.
Provide architectural leadership across cloud services, applications, APIs, networking, identity, databases, storage, observability, and integrations while establishing architecture standards, reference patterns, governance, and technical review processes.
Partner with engineering to improve deployment safety, performance, and readiness, driving automation, configuration management, and infrastructure as code.
Lead capacity planning for growth and demand spikes, eliminating single points of failure, undocumented systems, manual processes, and single-source dependencies.
Ensure production and nonproduction environments are properly separated, secured, and monitored, reviewing new systems for architectural fit, supportability, security, and total cost of ownership.
Establish and maintain service-level indicators (SLIs), SLOs, availability targets, and error-budget practices for critical systems.
Improve observability through centralized logging, metrics, distributed tracing, application performance monitoring (APM), and actionable alerting.
Lead major incident management, coordination, executive communication, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action tracking to improve mean time to detect, respond, and recover.
Develop and test backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity procedures, and establish sustainable on-call practices.
Own strategy and tooling for bot mitigation, scraping protection, automated abuse prevention, and traffic-quality management using technologies such as Cloudflare, DataDome, web application firewalls (WAFs), rate limiting, CAPTCHA alternatives, and device fingerprinting.
Partner with cross-functional teams to distinguish malicious automation from legitimate customers, search engines, partners, and approved AI crawlers, establishing monitoring and response procedures.
Oversee internal IT services and helpdesk support, establishing service-level expectations for response times, resolution times, user satisfaction, and backlog reduction.
Manage the employee technology lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, equipment provisioning, access management, asset recovery, and device inventory.
Standardize endpoint configuration, encryption, patching, and endpoint detection across laptops, collaboration platforms, productivity software, and telecom services.
Establish consistent identity and access management practices across corporate and production systems, implementing role-based access, least privilege, multi-factor authentication (MFA), periodic access reviews, and secure administrative account handling.
Support vulnerability remediation, security assessments, audits, vendor reviews, incident readiness, and applicable privacy requirements in partnership with legal and security teams.
Manage infrastructure, security, IT, telecom, monitoring, and support vendors, handling evaluations, contract reviews, renewals, licensing, service level agreements (SLAs), and budget management.
Improve cloud cost visibility through tagging, allocation, forecasting, tool consolidation, and contract optimization.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, SRE, platform engineering, DevOps, IT operations, or related disciplines.
5+ years of experience leading engineering or technology teams, including managing managers or technical leads.
Demonstrated experience operating high-traffic, customer-facing platforms in AWS or a comparable cloud environment.
Strong understanding of cloud architecture, networking, identity, security, observability, databases, APIs, storage, and distributed systems.
Experience managing production availability, incident response, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Experience with infrastructure automation, configuration management, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code.
Experience managing corporate IT, employee support, endpoint management, software licensing, and access provisioning.
Experience establishing operational metrics, SLOs, and support standards.
Demonstrated ability to manage vendors, contracts, departmental budgets, and cloud costs.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical risks, architecture, and tradeoffs to executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Cloudflare, DataDome, or comparable bot-management and web application protection platforms, including leading bot mitigation or traffic-quality programs.
Experience with AWS services, containerized environments, infrastructure as code, centralized logging, and APM tools (such as AppDynamics).
Experience supporting large-scale consumer subscription, public-record, data-as-a-service, advertising, or ecommerce platforms.
Experience modernizing legacy infrastructure, transitioning systems from external vendors, and consolidating cloud accounts or IT services.
Familiarity with privacy requirements and secure handling of sensitive consumer data.
Experience building or maturing SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering functions.

Measures of Success

Improved availability, performance, and stability of customer-facing platforms.
Reduced impact and infrastructure costs associated with bots, scraping, and automated abuse.
Faster incident detection, response, and recovery, alongside a reduction in recurring incidents.
Enhanced observability with reduced alert noise, validated disaster recovery capabilities, and optimized cloud spend.
Consistent helpdesk performance, reliable onboarding and offboarding, and robust endpoint security and asset tracking.
Strong architecture governance, reduced dependency on undocumented systems or vendors, and demonstrated team development.

Compensation and Benefits

Annual base salary: $170,000 - $180,000

Comprehensive health coverage including medical, dental, and vision insurance
Life insurance
Retirement benefits with employer match

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Engineering
jobs.description:
Who You’ll Work With

Reports to: 
Director, Infrastructure & Endpoint Services
We are looking for a seasoned, hands-on technical leader to join our team as Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Engineering. This high-impact role is responsible for driving strategy, prioritization, and execution across systems, cloud, and network engineering. You will lead a team of five engineers and partner closely with Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, and Support to deliver reliable, scalable, and secure infrastructure.
The right person for this role is comfortable setting technical direction while staying close to the work; partnering directly with the team to deliver results. You thrive in environments where strong people, processes, and infrastructure matter equally.
What You’ll Do

People Leadership

Lead, mentor, and support the professional development and career growth of a team of five engineers spanning systems, cloud, and network disciplines.
Build a culture of collaboration and continuous improvement, creating an environment where engineers can do their best work.
Conduct regular 1:1s to provide coaching, feedback, and guidance; establish clear performance expectations and accountability.
Manage team capacity to ensure the team is positioned for long-term success.
Partner with the Director of Infrastructure & Endpoint Services to align team goals with broader organizational strategy.

Technical Strategy & Execution

Assess, prioritize, and drive delivery of infrastructure initiatives across systems engineering, cloud platforms, and network infrastructure.
Serve as a technical thought leader, contributing to architectural decisions, reviewing solutions, and participating directly in hands-on work when needed.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Information Security to ensure infrastructure design, operations, and access management meet security and compliance requirements.
Collaborate with the Support team and other partner teams to act as a point of escalation for critical infrastructure issues and outages; including on-call management.
Define and monitor operational metrics including service availability, reliability, incident response, and project delivery.
Champion automation, documentation, and process improvements to drive operational efficiency across all functional areas of the team.

Portfolio & Project Management

Own and manage the infrastructure project portfolio, including intake, prioritization, planning, and delivery tracking.
Build and facilitate project and portfolio management practices using tools like Jira, ensuring visibility and accountability across the team.
Communicate project status, risks, and milestones clearly and consistently to stakeholders, including the Director of Infrastructure & Endpoint Services.
Drive on-time, high-quality delivery by helping the team break down complex initiatives into actionable work.

What You’ll Bring

A proven track record of success leading infrastructure engineering teams — including hands-on engineering experience in one or more of the following: cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), systems engineering, or network infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience managing and developing engineers, with a genuine commitment to mentorship and career development.
Strong proficiency with project and portfolio management — including practical experience with tools like Jira and the ability to build and sustain PM practices across a team.
Experience partnering cross-functionally with teams such as Information Security, IT Support, and business stakeholders to deliver complex infrastructure programs.
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field — or equivalent professional experience. Relevant certifications (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.) are a plus.

Technologies and Tools

Experience or familiarity with the following tools and platforms is a plus:
Cloud Platforms: AWS, Azure, GCP, Snowflake
Networking: Palo Alto, HP/Aruba
Project Management: Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow
Monitoring & Security: LogicMonitor, Rapid7
Productivity & Collaboration: Microsoft 365
Automation: IaC, Python, PowerShell, Bash, AWS CLI

About Us

Slalom is a fiercely human business and technology consulting company that leads with outcomes to bring more value, in all ways, always. From strategy through delivery, our agile teams across 52 offices in 12 countries partner with clients to co-create powerful customer experiences, modern ways of working, and meaningful impact. 
What sets us apart? We believe work should be challenging and fulfilling, not perfect, but possible. That’s why we prioritize purpose, flexibility, connection, and recognition, so our people can thrive and love what they do, most days. 
Compensation and Benefits

Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, parental leave, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and short/long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses, as well as discounted home, auto, and pet insurance.
Slalom is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. For this role, we are hiring at the following levels and targeted base pay salary ranges: The targeted base salary pay range for this position is $150,000 to 175,000. In addition, individuals may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. Actual compensation will depend upon an individual’s skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors. The salary pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time.    
We are committed to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws. If you have questions or concerns about the pay range or other compensation information in this posting, please contact us at: peopleone@slalom.com.
EEO and Accommodations

Slalom is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to attracting, developing and retaining highly qualified talent who empower our innovative teams through unique perspectives and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Slalom will also consider qualified applications with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Slalom welcomes and encourages applications from individuals with disabilities. Reasonable accommodations are available for candidates during all aspects of the selection process. Please advise the talent acquisition team or contact accomodationrequest@slalom.com if you require accommodations during the interview process.

jobs.title: Group Senior Manager, Infrastructure
jobs.description:
The Group Infrastructure Manager is accountable for the strategy, governance, and overall performance of the Group’s IT infrastructure environment, spanning networks, servers, cloud platforms, end-user computing, workplace collaboration, and infrastructure security. Reporting to the IDT Director, the Manager owns the Group’s infrastructure and cloud roadmap, the infrastructure budget, and the vendor and service-provider portfolio, and is accountable for the reliability, security, scalability, and cost-effectiveness of infrastructure services across all Group sites. The incumbent leads and develops a team of infrastructure and site-reliability professionals, sets technical direction, standards, and policies, drives cloud adoption and automation, and represents infrastructure to senior management and regional stakeholders — ensuring infrastructure capabilities are aligned with, and enable, the Group’s digital transformation agenda.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Strategic Planning and Predictive Readiness

Develop, own, and govern the Group’s infrastructure and cloud roadmap, ensuring network, cloud, collaboration, and security investments are aligned with business priorities and the Group’s digital strategy.
Define infrastructure standards, architecture principles, and policies, and ensure consistent adoption across all Group sites.
Lead capacity planning, technology refresh, and lifecycle management to anticipate future business requirements, mitigate operational risk, and prevent technology obsolescence.
Own the annual infrastructure budget, including capital and operating expenditure — securing funding, controlling spend, and ensuring value for money.
Establish, govern, and periodically review IT disaster-recovery and business-continuity plans for critical infrastructure services.
Evaluate emerging technologies — cloud services, AIOps, automation, workplace collaboration, and cybersecurity and make investment recommendations where they deliver measurable business value.

Operational and Service Accountability

Hold overall accountability for the availability, performance, security, and cost-efficiency of all infrastructure services against agreed KPIs and SLAs.
Govern incident, problem, and change management, ensuring major incidents are resolved, root causes addressed, and service stability maintained.
Provide governance and assurance over infrastructure projects, ensuring delivery within approved scope, timeline, budget, and quality.
Direct the management and optimisation of the Group’s cloud platforms to enhance scalability, security, resilience, performance, and cost efficiency.
Ensure AIOps, observability, and site-reliability capabilities are developed and matured to drive proactive, resilient operations.
Ensure infrastructure security, patch management, backup operations, and compliance activities are executed in accordance with Group IT policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.

People, Vendor and Commercial Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the infrastructure and site-reliability team — setting objectives, managing performance, and building capability and succession.
Own vendor and service-provider relationships and contracts, including selection, negotiation, commercial management, and SLA governance to secure quality, accountability, and value-for-money outcomes.
Represent infrastructure to the IDT Director, senior management, and regional stakeholders, providing assurance, insight, and recommendations.

Reporting and Insight

Oversee monitoring and reporting of infrastructure availability, performance, capacity, utilisation, risk, and service levels against agreed KPIs and SLAs.
Translate operational and performance trends into management insight and decisions on capacity planning, cost optimisation, service improvement, and risk mitigation.
Ensure accurate asset records, configuration information, infrastructure documentation, and operational procedures are maintained by the team.

EXPERIENCE:
Minimum experience in IT infrastructure of 12 years in a managerial role with accountability for teams, budgets, and vendor contracts.
Proven track record owning and governing infrastructure and cloud strategy, roadmaps, and standards across multiple sites or countries.
Strong experience managing infrastructure budgets (capital and operating), vendor selection, contract negotiation, and commercial governance.
Experience leading cloud adoption and transformation across platforms (e.g. Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Microsoft 365) and hybrid environments.
Experience embedding AIOps, observability, or site-reliability engineering (SRE) and ITIL service management at an organisational level.
Solid grounding in infrastructure security, backup and disaster recovery, IT governance, and regulatory compliance.
Broad experience administering or governing workplace-collaboration platforms (e.g. Microsoft 365, Teams, or Google Workspace). Experience leading multi-site or regional operations, ideally within a manufacturing or industrial environment.

new_jobs.description:
The Group Infrastructure Manager is accountable for the strategy, governance, and overall performance of the Group’s IT infrastructure environment, spanning networks, servers, cloud platforms, end-user computing, workplace collaboration, and infrastructure security. The incumbent leads and develops a team of infrastructure and site-reliability professionals, sets technical direction, standards, and policies, drives cloud adoption and automation, and represents infrastructure to senior management and regional stakeholders — ensuring infrastructure capabilities are aligned with, and enable, the Group’s digital transformation agenda.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Strategic Planning and Predictive Readiness

Develop, own, and govern the Group’s infrastructure and cloud roadmap, ensuring network, cloud, collaboration, and security investments are aligned with business priorities and the Group’s digital strategy.
Define infrastructure standards, architecture principles, and policies, and ensure consistent adoption across all Group sites.
Lead capacity planning, technology refresh, and lifecycle management to anticipate future business requirements, mitigate operational risk, and prevent technology obsolescence.
Own the annual infrastructure budget, including capital and operating expenditure — securing funding, controlling spend, and ensuring value for money.
Establish, govern, and periodically review IT disaster-recovery and business-continuity plans for critical infrastructure services.
Evaluate emerging technologies — cloud services, AIOps, automation, workplace collaboration, and cybersecurity and make investment recommendations where they deliver measurable business value.

Operational and Service Accountability

Hold overall accountability for the availability, performance, security, and cost-efficiency of all infrastructure services against agreed KPIs and SLAs.
Govern incident, problem, and change management, ensuring major incidents are resolved, root causes addressed, and service stability maintained.
Provide governance and assurance over infrastructure projects, ensuring delivery within approved scope, timeline, budget, and quality.
Direct the management and optimisation of the Group’s cloud platforms to enhance scalability, security, resilience, performance, and cost efficiency.
Ensure AIOps, observability, and site-reliability capabilities are developed and matured to drive proactive, resilient operations.
Ensure infrastructure security, patch management, backup operations, and compliance activities are executed in accordance with Group IT policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.

People, Vendor and Commercial Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the infrastructure and site-reliability team — setting objectives, managing performance, and building capability and succession.
Own vendor and service-provider relationships and contracts, including selection, negotiation, commercial management, and SLA governance to secure quality, accountability, and value-for-money outcomes.
Represent infrastructure to the IDT Director, senior management, and regional stakeholders, providing assurance, insight, and recommendations.

Reporting and Insight

Oversee monitoring and reporting of infrastructure availability, performance, capacity, utilisation, risk, and service levels against agreed KPIs and SLAs.
Translate operational and performance trends into management insight and decisions on capacity planning, cost optimisation, service improvement, and risk mitigation.
Ensure accurate asset records, configuration information, infrastructure documentation, and operational procedures are maintained by the team.

EXPERIENCE:
Minimum experience in IT infrastructure of 12 years in a managerial role with accountability for teams, budgets, and vendor contracts.
Proven track record owning and governing infrastructure and cloud strategy, roadmaps, and standards across multiple sites or countries.
Strong experience managing infrastructure budgets (capital and operating), vendor selection, contract negotiation, and commercial governance.
Experience leading cloud adoption and transformation across platforms (e.g. Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Microsoft 365) and hybrid environments.
Experience embedding AIOps, observability, or site-reliability engineering (SRE) and ITIL service management at an organisational level.
Solid grounding in infrastructure security, backup and disaster recovery, IT governance, and regulatory compliance.
Broad experience administering or governing workplace-collaboration platforms (e.g. Microsoft 365, Teams, or Google Workspace). Experience leading multi-site or regional operations, ideally within a manufacturing or industrial environment.

new_jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a hands-on, multi-disciplinary Chief Technology Officer to lead its end-to-end technology organization, spanning product engineering, IT infrastructure, and corporate and platform cybersecurity.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and partnering with executive leadership, this executive provides comprehensive oversight across technology, enterprise systems, and risk management. The Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer reports directly to this role.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Drive overall technology strategy, cloud infrastructure, and technical execution for the organization's core SaaS platform.
Manage the enterprise technology budget and drive cost optimization across software licensing, infrastructure procurement, hardware lifecycles, and vendor contracts.
Partner with executive leadership to transition new products from beta to market launch while actively managing technical debt.
Advise the CEO and Board of Directors on enterprise technical risk, disaster recovery, business continuity planning, and corporate cyber resilience.
Oversee day-to-day corporate IT operations, including endpoint management, automated provisioning and deprovisioning, and multi-tier helpdesk support.
Administer enterprise productivity suites and communication architectures while enforcing zero-trust access controls, single sign-on (SSO), and document retention policies.
Oversee business system infrastructure in close alignment with organizational leadership to ensure high uptime and integration security.
Direct organization-wide information security initiatives across corporate endpoints, networks, and SaaS tools.
Establish and audit enterprise IT policies, including acceptable use, zero-trust identity and access management (IAM), data loss prevention (DLP), and offboarding protocols.
Enforce compliance and audit readiness—including SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, ISO 27001, and c3/c4 non-profit legal boundaries—in collaboration with Legal, HR, and Finance.
Evaluate alpha projects and proofs of concept across departments, guiding execution to integrate them into the core SaaS platform or architect them as standalone, scalable services.
Mitigate vendor lock-in risk by establishing standardized data portability and integration frameworks across corporate SaaS applications.
Serve as direct manager to the Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer (CPEDO), establishing shared goals and aligning product, engineering, and data strategies with enterprise infrastructure and security standards.
Partner with the CPEDO on budget, resourcing, and prioritization trade-offs across product, engineering, and data initiatives.
Build, mentor, and scale a service-oriented IT and security team aligned with organizational growth objectives.
Establish pragmatic automated internal processes that maintain rigorous security standards without introducing operational friction for staff.

Qualifications

12+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, including roles such as Director of IT, Head of IT/Operations Technology, VP of IT, or Chief Technology Officer.
Demonstrated experience managing enterprise IT and information security stacks, zero-trust architectures, IAM, and automated endpoint management.
Experience driving capital and operational expenditure (CapEx/OpEx) strategies for corporate IT, including SaaS license management, hardware procurement cycles, and third-party vendor governance.
Proven track record leading enterprise security operations and successfully navigating SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 audit cycles.
Expertise in architecting, securing, and administering enterprise collaboration platforms and workplace productivity suites.
Proven track record of building and leading technical teams across a broad range of expertise.
Experience building or scaling an internal IT function through periods of organizational growth.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical staff, executive leadership, and Board members.

Compensation and Benefits

Annual salary: $220,000 to $230,000,
commensurate with experience.
Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Healthcare Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) options.
403(b) retirement plan with an employer match.
Paid vacation, paid holidays, and paid sick leave.
Paid parental leave.
Professional development and education reimbursement assistance.
Monthly technology and wellness stipend.
